title: A constructed real bounded away from zero has a multiplicative inverse
statement: For a constructed real x and a natural n witnessing x is positively bounded away from zero at precision n (CReal.PosBound x n), x * x^-1 is CReal.Equiv-equivalent to 1, where the inverse is built from the witness n. Unlike ℚ's total mul_inv_cancel_of_ne_zero, ℝ's inverse is PARTIAL and the witness is data -- see the pre-existing F:real-inverse-is-partial-and-its-modulus-is-data, which states this for the axiomatized AxReal package; this fact pins the same shape for the constructed carrier the shipped route actually reasons over.

formal.statement: theorem CReal.mul_inv_cancel : ((x0 : CReal) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : CReal.PosBound x0 x1) -> CReal.Equiv (CReal.mul x0 (CReal.inv x0 x1 x2)) CReal.one)))

evidence.supports: CReal.mul_inv_cancel is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example theorem_dependency_inventory -- CReal.mul_inv_cancel 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '^CReal\.mul_inv_cancel[[:space:]]'
evidence.notes: `build_creal_prelude` admits CReal.mul_inv_cancel through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate, which re-checks the proof term against the stated type, so a line in this tool's output for the exact name is a machine-checked proof having been admitted. `theorem_dependency_inventory` was extended in this same change to build creal/complex/cpoint (previously only nat/integer/rat/string/characterization); it exits non-zero for a named filter that matches nothing, and `grep -c` (never `-q`) independently asserts the exact tab-anchored line is present. `--release` is MANDATORY: building the constructed carriers recurses deep enough in a debug build to overflow the default thread stack (measured: release exits 0 with 1092 theorems total, debug SIGABRTs at 134) -- the same resource-limit gotcha already documented for `prelude_theorem_inventory --include-constructed`.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the CReal prelude's trusted surface is empty
evidence.notes: `nat_axiom_inventory --include-constructed` builds the CReal environment as its own group and reports `creal: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0 total_trusted=0` (re-measured on this tree). That bounds every individual CReal theorem's footprint by [], since a theorem cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain, and the enumeration covers Axiom, Opaque AND Quotient, not just Declaration::Axiom. `--include-constructed` is REQUIRED here -- without it `--require-axiom-free creal` is an error (verified: exit 1), not a silent pass, because creal is not built at all without the flag; this is the standing trap of an empty/absent result reading as a strong negative when the tool was never pointed at the subject.
